# `TEAM.md`'s seating chart are GENERATED from it — run `pnpm guard:seats --write-table` and

# > **Registry read:** last verified 2026-08-24 · review every 7 days
# WHY A FRESHNESS LINE. CI cannot read either scheduler, so this file is a SNAPSHOT taken by a
# session that can. The line above is what forces someone to re-take it. Going stale is itself a
# failure — that is the whole point, because a roster nobody re-measures is how ten seats came to
#   CCR fleet   : RemoteTrigger action:list      (MCP, cloud only) — FILTER cron_expression != ""
#                 The list is dominated by ephemeral one-shot PR-watchers that carry an empty
#                 cron and a run_once_at. They are not seats. Only cron rows belong here.
# Then bump the date above, run `pnpm guard:seats --write-table`, and commit both.
# CCR READ COMPLETED 2026-08-24 — this supersedes the "two pages were sampled" caveat that
# shipped with #722. The full trigger list was read and filtered to cron_expression != "":
#   25 triggers total · 20 recurring · 5 ephemeral one-shot PR-watchers (correctly excluded)
#   Of the 20 recurring: 18 are Homiquity seats and are recorded below.
#   The other 2 are deliberately NOT seats and are named here so 20 vs 18 reconciles instead
#   of reading as fresh drift: "Sunday travel + calendar brief" (trig_01Suy9wpSzy5MSV2JvAcekKX)
#   and "Barakat RE — daily inbox triage" (trig_017g5xqR4fX63FyivX7dvnQM). Both are enabled,
#   both belong to other work, neither writes to this repo.
# Enabled at that read: 8 of 20. The 12 paused ones carry NO ended_reason and NO
# suspension_reason, which per the scheduler means switched off by hand — not expired, not
#   unregistered is a FIRST-CLASS state, not an omission. CHARTER §11: "a definition on disk that
#   is not registered in the scheduler is not a routine — it is a fossil, and fossils are what
#   produced §0." The roster must be able to say that out loud.
# statusReason + reviewBy are REQUIRED for paused/unregistered/unverified. A pause with no expiry
#   is the DA-0820-09 failure: a control paused because of a premise dies when the premise
